disposition_mapping.rationale: Claim submission persists as the entry point of the target workflow and still requires receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold (EXR-R-01, EXR-R-10), now combined with automated receipt capture.
Receipt capture and extraction is unconstrained by design and is automated into real-time OCR at the point of submission, removing a separate manual AP analyst handoff while preserving the function.

The policy compliance check must survive in some form (EXR-R-07) and must still precede line manager approval (EXR-R-02). It is restructured into a rules-engine check with AP analyst review limited to flagged exceptions, retaining its gatekeeping function and sequence.

Line manager approval must survive in some form (EXR-R-08), remain performed by an actor distinct from the submitter (EXR-R-03), and precede reimbursement (EXR-R-06). It is retained unchanged as a discrete human decision step.

Finance review is unconstrained by design and is merged with posting into a single exception-based review-and-post step, scoping manual finance effort to flagged items (coding, exceptions, evidence gaps) while unflagged claims post straight-through.

Posting continues to consume the expense transaction date (EXR-R-04) and the transaction-date exchange rate (EXR-R-05) per IAS 21 (KB-07, KB-08), now automated and combined with the finance review step so that coding review and posting occur in one pass.
Reimbursement must survive in some form (EXR-R-09) and must still follow line manager approval (EXR-R-06); it is retained as the payment step, merged with notification for efficiency.
Employee notification is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into the payment run as an automated confirmation triggered on payment completion, removing a separate manual notification task.

steps.description: The employee submits an out-of-pocket expense claim through a mobile/web tool that performs OCR capture and data extraction on attached receipts in real time, producing a structured claim record at the point of submission. Receipts remain mandatory for claim lines above the receipt threshold.
inputs: Receipts for claim lines above the receipt threshold
steps.name: Claim submission with automated receipt capture

steps.description: A rules engine checks every claim line against expense policy limits, categories and per diem rates. Lines that pass are auto-cleared; lines that fail or fall outside system confidence (e.g. missing receipt, unusual category, duplicate suspicion) are routed to an AP analyst for exception review before the claim proceeds to approval.
steps.name: Automated policy compliance check with exception review

steps.description: The claimant's line manager approves or rejects the policy-checked claim. This step remains a distinct human decision performed by an actor other than the claim submitter.
steps.name: Line manager approval

steps.description: Approved claims flow to an automated posting engine that codes expense accounts and cost centres and translates foreign-currency lines using the transaction-date exchange rate, posting in the period the expense was incurred. A finance reviewer examines only claims flagged for coding anomalies, policy exceptions or insufficient supporting evidence before or alongside posting; unflagged claims post straight-through.
steps.name: Finance exception review and automated posting

steps.description: The approved claim is paid to the employee through the AP payment run, and the employee is automatically notified of payment once the run completes, eliminating a separate manual notification step.
steps.name: Reimbursement via AP payment run with automated employee notification
